summary: Security retest after SEC-001/2/3 fixes. Added 20 new tests covering: scoped /api/procesos & /api/procesos/{id}/anforas for operator/validator, 403 enforcement on /resumen, /resultado-universitario, /recintos, /mesas, /estructura, /agregacion, unauthenticated access, image-token protection, and public draft isolation. 38/41 passed, 2 skipped (no non-locked image available in dataset — limitation documented, no OCR performed as instructed), 1 FAILED exposing a NEW privilege-escalation regression on /api/admin/usuarios-operativos. Frontend smoke OK: TREP desktop & resultados-publicos (desktop + mobile) only expose the locked acta; the unblocked draft on the other anfora is NOT visible publicly.

critical.issue: SEC-REGRESSION / privilege escalation: endpoint uses `Depends(usuario_actual)` instead of `Depends(requerir_admin)`. Any logged-in operator can create new operational users (verified: operator token → 200 OK with new user id). Fix: change line 796 of /app/backend/server.py from `usuario: dict = Depends(usuario_actual)` to `admin: dict = Depends(requerir_admin)` (and remove the unused reassignment of `usuario` below).

issues: Recharts still logs width/height(-1) warnings on initial render — non-blocking (carried over from iteration 1).

action_items: CRITICAL: fix /api/admin/usuarios-operativos to require admin (`Depends(requerir_admin)`); currently any authenticated operator/validator can create more operational users (privilege escalation). This is a regression from recent audit changes.
Optional: add a brute-force lockout on /api/auth/login (noted in iteration 1, still absent).
Optional: split server.py (>2400 lines) into routers for maintainability.

/api/resumen/{id}, /api/procesos/{id}/resultado-universitario are gated by `requerir_resultados` (admin|resultados) — operator & validator get 403 (verified).

Author-cannot-validate / self-cannot-block policy still enforced through `_autorizar_anfora_operativa` + funcion filtering — verified.
DELETE /api/admin/asignaciones-operativas/{id} is correctly admin-gated and verified in cleanup.

rca of the issue: Root cause of the privilege-escalation finding: during the recent security audit, the `/api/admin/usuarios-operativos` POST endpoint’s dependency was weakened from `requerir_admin` to `usuario_actual` (server.py line 796). All other `/api/admin/*` POSTs in the file use `requerir_admin`, so this is clearly a localised regression and not a design decision. Reproduction: `POST /api/auth/login` as operador@stre.bo, use the Bearer token on `POST /api/admin/usuarios-operativos` with a valid payload (contrasena ≥10 chars, nombre_completo ≥3 chars) → returns 200 + new user id. Mitigation: change the dependency to `admin: dict = Depends(requerir_admin)` and rename the local variable to avoid shadowing. After the fix, re-run `pytest backend/tests/backend_test.py::TestBolaRead::test_non_admin_cannot_create_users -n 0` — expected 403.
